rationale: Published clinical summaries of Jaberi-Elahi syndrome indicate that skeletal abnormalities (including scoliosis, kyphoscoliosis, and contractures) occur in 23 of 28 individuals (~82.1%), who predominantly harbor biallelic truncating (nonsense, frameshift, splice-site) variants in GTPBP2. In contrast, Manoochehri et al. (2024) described a 3-year-old patient homozygous for a novel missense variant (p.Leu430Pro) who completely lacked skeletal abnormalities. A potential confounding factor is age-dependent penetrance, as spinal deformities often manifest or worsen after prolonged hypotonia or spasticity.

evidence.text: In a systematic review of 28 individuals with Jaberi-Elahi syndrome, 23 of 28 (82.1%) presented with skeletal problems (such as scoliosis and kyphoscoliosis). In contrast, the reported 3-year-old proband homozygous for a novel missense variant (p.Leu430Pro) did not exhibit any skeletal abnormalities.

source.quote: A large numbers of patients manifest motor development delay (26/28), sparse hair (26/28), and speech disorder (24/28). Moreover, a significant fraction of patients suffer from intellectual disability (23/28), hypotonia (23/28), skeletal problems (23/28), and visual impairment (18/28). In spite of previous patients, the proband in this study did not exhibit any skeletal abnormalities.

new_directions.question_text: Is the absence of skeletal abnormalities in missense GTPBP2 cases caused by residual protein function or due to young age at evaluation?
new_directions.rationale: Kyphoscoliosis and joint contractures often develop progressively secondary to chronic hypotonia or spasticity; longitudinal assessment of missense variant carriers across older ages is required to determine whether skeletal sparing persists into adolescence and adulthood.
